prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Phoenix after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Phoenix for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but I want to be careful: I don’t have live web access right now, so I can’t pull an up‑to‑date phonebook of Phoenix firms. I can, however, give you exactly what you need to find the best attorneys quickly and safely: where to look, which specific types of firms to call, a short script and the key questions to ask, and the red flags to avoid. If you want, I can then look up current phone numbers or confirm firm reputations if you paste a few names or let me know you’ll allow web lookups.

Quick summary — who to call first
- One large national plaintiff firm with local presence (good for big resources and investigators).
- One or two well‑established Phoenix boutique personal injury firms that focus on car crashes and have trial experience.
- One local attorney with strong recent verdicts or settlements (good if your case may go to trial).
If you tell me whether you prefer a big firm vs a small local firm, or how severe your injuries are, I’ll tailor names.

Where to find reputable Phoenix personal injury lawyers right now
- Arizona State Bar Lawyer Referral Service — official and reliable.
- Avvo and Martindale‑Hubbell — show ratings, peer reviews and disciplinary records.
- Google and Yelp — read recent client reviews; look for consistent recent positive feedback.
- Local courthouse records — search for recent verdicts and which attorneys tried cases.
- Better Business Bureau — check for complaints and responses.

What to look for when choosing a firm
- Focus: they primarily handle personal injury/car accidents.
- Trial experience: they’ve actually taken cases to jury trial (not all firms settle everything).
- Track record: recent settlements/verdicts in Arizona, ideally similar crashes/injuries.
- Contingency fee: most PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover).
- Communication: they answer quickly and explain things clearly.
- Resources: access to accident reconstruction, medical experts, and investigators if needed.
- Local reputation and no disciplinary issues with the State Bar.

Questions to ask on the first call (takes 10–15 minutes)
1. Do you handle car accident/personal injury cases in Phoenix full time?  
2. How long have you practiced personal injury law in Arizona?  
3. Do you handle cases on contingency? What is your contingency fee and are there any other costs I might owe?  
4. How many cases like mine have you handled recently? What were typical results?  
5. Will you personally handle my case or will other attorneys/paralegals? Who will be my primary contact?  
6. Do you have trial experience and have you taken cases to verdict in Maricopa County?  
7. What is your estimate of how long my case might take?  
8. How do you communicate (phone/email/text) and how often will I get updates?  
9. Do you have resources for accident reconstruction and medical expert witnesses?  
10. Can you give references from recent clients or outcomes for similar cases?

Red flags to avoid
- High‑pressure “sign today” tactics or promises of a specific amount before seeing records.  
- Unwillingness to put fee terms in writing.  
- Poor communication on initial contact (don’t ignore prompt responsiveness).  
- Negative State Bar record or lots of unresolved consumer complaints.

What to have ready for the call
- Date/time/location of crash, brief description of what happened.  
- Photos of the vehicles or scene, if you have them.  
- Names of any witnesses and the other driver’s insurance.  
- Brief list of injuries and medical visits/records.  
- Any police report number.

Immediate actions after the accident (if you haven’t already)
- Get all medical care needed — document everything.  
- Preserve photos, videos, and damaged parts of the vehicle.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without a lawyer.  
- Note witnesses and get contact info.  
- Keep all bills and time‑off records.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short list of specific firms (national and local) to call if you tell me whether you prefer a big firm, a local boutique, or a trial‑focused attorney.  
- Draft a short phone script you can read when you call.  
- Review any firms you’ve already found (just paste the names/links) and point out pros/cons.

Which would you prefer: a shortlist now (and tell me big firm vs boutique), or help searching and vetting firms you already found?
